messages:
sam: Quick follow-up on observability/cost attribution idea: propose an "attribute capsule" that travels with requests. Its like a compact, structured header that can be hashed/bucketed to avoid high-cardinality explosion. want feedback before a full RFC.

rachel: TL;DR: capsule = header with low-card keys + optional signed proof?

sam: Exactly. Two main properties: small fixed schema (slots), and an optional HMAC signature when gateway asserts authority. Example header:```Attribute-Capsule: v1;slots=app:checkout,env:prod,cost_bucket:42;sig=base64(hmac)```The cost_bucket is derived by hashing the raw tenant id into N buckets at the ingress (deterministic, low-cardinality).

vik: how do we handle late-enrich? lots of services add user_id or session_id later. We must avoid indexing those.

sam: Plan: capsule has typed slots: anchor (indexed, low-card), bucket (pre-hashed), opaque (stored but not indexed). Late-enrich can attach opaque slots to span envelope but they aren't eligible for billing queries.

rachel: What about spoofing? If downstream services can set capsule header, they could fake billing attribution.

sam: Two mitigations: 1) gateways and edge proxies inject signed capsule when they own the request path (sig present). Ingest will prefer signed capsule for billing. 2) we keep a trust-tier header (X-Capsule-Source) and only allow certain sources to provide signed capsules. Unsigned capsules are treated as advisory and not used for cost attribution.

vik: Nice. Also need a migration path for existing billing_key. Suggest we compute bucket from billing_key and populate capsule.bucket at gateway. That keeps existing billing pipeline mostly unchanged.

sam: Agreed. Add a compatibility mode that copies billing_key->capsule.bucket and marks capsule as signed when gateway sees valid billing token.

rachel: Sampling implications? If we sample before gateway, we might lose capsule. We should ensure capsule read happens pre-sampling or capsule is duplicated into the sampling metadata.

sam: Correct. Ingest order: read capsule header, record anchor/bucket into sampling metadata, then make sampling decision. That guarantees billing tags survive sampling. Late-enrich remains for debug only.

vik: Query side: we shouldn't open arbitrary new filter fields. Proposal: expose only anchor and bucket as queryable columns. Provide a raw payload lookup endpoint for opaque fields.

sam: Yep. Query engine change minimal: map capsule.anchor -> column, capsule.bucket -> column. Opaque in JSON blob for ad-hoc. We'll also add a helper to resolve bucket->approx-tenant for debugging (best effort).

rachel: Ops/runbook: what are circuit breakers if cardinality spikes?

sam: ingestion controls: per-tenant slot quota, daily cardinality cap, auto-demote new distinct values to "_unknown" when threshold exceeded. Also telemetry: ingest rate + cardinality alarm.

vik: we should run a perf matrix: synthetic bullets: 1M spans/day with 3 anchor values vs 100k anchors. i'll simulate index growth + query latency.

sre-bot: perf-scheduler: queued test 4490002000 'capsule-index-growth' (est 3h). results will post to channel when done.

rachel: Any impact on logs? Are we also injecting capsule into structured logs to correlate traces+logs?

sam: Good idea. Plan is to mirror capsule into log record as minimal fields (anchor,bucket). No opaque fields in logs. That keeps log index safe.

vik: Security note: HMAC sig key rotation and key provenance needs callouts in RFC. Also what to do when signature verification fails? fallback to unsigned handling and alert.

sam: will include key rotation, verification policy, and a small shim: unknown-sig -> treat as advisory + trace flagged for manual review.

rachel: Sounds actionable. Please include a couple of concrete examples in RFC and a rollout checklist (gateway change, ingest schema update, query mapping, perf tests, ops alarms).

sam: will do. I'll draft RFC with concrete header spec, bucket hash algorithm (Murmur3 -> modulo N), HMAC scheme, sampling order, ingest caps, and migration steps. tagging @eng-platform for review. :rocket:
